ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.claim: Verses 15–21 explain the traits of those cast into Hell and those shielded from it, together with their reward.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r7.anchor: An explanation of the character of people who will be thrown into Hell and those who will be shielded from it

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r4.claim: Spending that purifies wealth matters to God when done to please Him, without seeking repayment or gratitude, as 76:9 also says.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r4.anchor: spending in the way of God to purify one’s wealth has any significance in the eyes of God which is done to please Him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r5.speaker: some people
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r5.claim: Some render the verse as saying that the recipient had done no favour that obliges the giver to repay it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p351/r5.anchor: Some people have translated this verse as: “And no one has done him a favour for which he is obliged to repay it.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p352/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p352/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p352/r2.claim: Even if that rendering is linguistically possible, it cannot mean that repaying a benefactor is not God-pleasing; reciprocal kindness remains virtuous.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p352/r2.anchor: why should it not be counted as an act of virtue? If on one occasion, a poor person quenched another person’s thirst

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p352/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p352/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p352/r3.claim: Islahi prefers his own translation because it is linguistically sound and avoids the mistaken implication that reciprocal kindness cannot please God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p352/r3.anchor: Readers are advised to take another look

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r4.claim: The majority read ابتغاء in the accusative as a detached exception, since it is not part of the favor being repaid.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إلا ابتغاء بنصب الهمزة، وهو استثناء منقطع لأنه ليس داخلا في من نعمة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r5.speaker: ابن وثاب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r5.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads it in the nominative as a substitute for niʿma, a Tamīm dialect also illustrated by poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب: بالرفع على البدل في موضع نعمة لأنه رفع، وهي لغة تميم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r6.speaker: الزمخشري والفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī, following al-Farrāʾ, allows ابتغاء وجه الله as a purpose object: he gives to seek God's face, not repayment for a favor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p494/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ابتغاء وجه الله مفعولا له على المعنى

BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.claim: The oath's night, daylight, and creation frame divergent earthly endeavors, then contrasting afterlife fates: the denier's fire and the pious giver's satisfaction.
BINTSHATI:v2p121/r6.anchor: وعلى هذا النسق من البيان المعجز، يتم الربط بين المقسم به في أول السورة:

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r7.claim: The giver seeks no repayment for anyone’s favor; the detached exception marks his sole aim as seeking his Lord’s pleasure.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r7.anchor: من نعمة تجزى * } أي هي مما يحق جزاؤه لأجلها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r8.claim: God’s “face” signifies His essence and the highest aim: the giver seeks neither worldly gain nor even an afterlife reward.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p449/r8.anchor: فلا نظر له إلا إلى ذاته سبحانه وتعالى التي عبر عنها بالوجه

NAHHAS:v5p243/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p243/r12.claim: The exception is disconnected according to Basrans; al-Farrāʾ also permits an implied clause or a nominative reading, but Abū Jaʿfar says that reading is unattested and remote.
NAHHAS:v5p243/r12.anchor: استثناء ليس من الأول لم يذكر البصريون غير هذا

NAHHAS:v5p243/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r13.speaker: الشاعر
NAHHAS:v5p243/r13.claim: An anonymous poet's example has gazelles and camels as the only exceptions in a land without people, illustrating a nominative exception.
NAHHAS:v5p243/r13.anchor: بلدة ليس بها أنيس … إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس

NAHHAS:v5p243/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r14.speaker: النابغة الذبياني
NAHHAS:v5p243/r14.claim: His poem supplies another example of a nominative exception after a negative clause.

NAHHAS:v5p243/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p243/r15.claim: Seeking God's face means seeking His pleasure; the nominative exception is a figurative construction.
NAHHAS:v5p243/r15.anchor: وهذا مجاز أي إلا طلب رضوانه

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.claim: Abu Qahafa urged freeing strong men who could protect Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr said he sought God's face, and the report says the passage through ‘he will be satisfied’ was revealed about him.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r4.anchor: وأخرج الحاكم وصححه عن عامر بن عبد الله بن الزبير عن أبيه

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r5.speaker: عامر بن الزبير عن أبيه
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r5.claim: A separate report says the closing verses about seeking God's face and being satisfied were revealed concerning Abu Bakr.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r5.anchor: وأخرج البزار وابن جرير وابن المنذر والطبراني وابن عدي وابن مردويه وابن عساكر من وجه آخر عن عامر بن الزبير عن أبيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r6.claim: Illa ibtigha is a disconnected exception, though Ibn Atiyya finds this grammatical analysis questionable.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p492/r6.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إلا ابتغاء نصب بالاستثناء المنقطع وفيه نظر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.claim: Many commentators say these verses were revealed about Abu Bakr, and some claim consensus; Ibn Kathir says Abu Bakr certainly falls within their general wording and is foremost in these virtues.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r5.anchor: ولا شك أنه داخل فيها، وأولى الأمة (5) بعمومها، فإن لفظها لفظ العموم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r6.claim: Abu Bakr gave generously for God's sake and to support the Messenger without owing repayment to anyone; even Arab leaders had received his beneficence.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r6.anchor: فكم من دراهم (6) ودنانير (7) بذلها ابتغاء وجه ربه الكريم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r7.claim: The Prophet says the gates of Paradise call to someone who spends two kinds of wealth in God's path; asked whether anyone is called from all gates, he tells Abu Bakr yes and hopes he will be among them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p422/r7.anchor: في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "من أنفق زوجين في سبيل الله دعته خزنة الجنة: يا عبد الله، هذا خير"

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r12.claim: Seeking the face of his Lord means seeking God's pleasure; “face” refers to God himself, and illā means “but.”
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r12.anchor: إلا ابتغاء؛ أي: طلب وجه ربه أي: رضا ربه، فذكر وجهه وأراد نفسه

JISHUMI:v10p7447/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r13.claim: Al-aʿlā means the one who overpowers everything, or it may mean the most exalted.
JISHUMI:v10p7447/r13.anchor: الأعلى أي: الأقدر الذي يقهر كل شيء ولا يمتنع، وقيل: الأعلى: الأجل

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.speaker: several commentators
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.claim: Commentators tell of a Medinan palm owner who snatched fallen dates from a poor family's children and refused the Prophet's offer of a Paradise palm; another man paid forty palms, donated the tree, and the Prophet gave it to the family. The refusal maps to vv. 15–16, the gift to vv. 18–21.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r1.anchor: Several commentators say that the whole of this sūrah was revealed in reference to a Muslim of Madinah who had a palm tree

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.claim: If this is an early Makkan sūrah, the palm-tree story likely is not its occasion; the verses instead generally condemn those who rejected Muhammad as prophet.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r2.anchor: If, however, this is an early Makkan sūrah, as some maintain

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.speaker: others
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.claim: Others say vv. 17–21 praise Abū Bakr, who bought and freed weak slaves; when his father asked why he did not buy stronger defenders, he said he sought no defense.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r4.anchor: others say that vv. 18–21 were revealed about the first Caliph, Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, who used to buy weak slaves and then free them

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.claim: One revelation account says Bilāl was tortured after desecrating the Kaʿbah idols, kept testifying to God's oneness, and the Prophet assured him that the One would save him.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r5.anchor: One account of the revelation of these verses states that, upon embracing Islam, Bilāl, who was a slave of one ʿAbd Allāh ibn Judan

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.claim: In that account Abū Bakr bought Bilāl for gold after the Prophet told him Bilāl was tortured for God; the idolaters alleged he acted to repay a favor, prompting vv. 19–21.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r6.anchor: The Prophet came upon this and said to him, “The One will save you!” He then informed Abū Bakr, saying,“Bilāl is being tortured for the sake of God!

STUDYQURAN:92:15/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r8.claim: The verse literally says no one has a favor with him to repay: he neither repays past favors nor expects future recompense, but gives only to seek God's will.
STUDYQURAN:92:15/r8.anchor: This verse literally reads, “no one having with him any favor to be repaid.” In both translations the implication is that one is neither recompensing others for favors

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.claim: The longer, central portrait of the pious clarifies that generosity is for ethical purification, not repayment of worldly favors, and is directed toward the Lord's face through a biblical metaphor.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r6.anchor: Der Gottesfürchtige gibt um seiner ethischen Reinheit willen (V. 18) und nicht aufgrund weltlicher Beweggründe wie der Rückerstattung empfangener Wohltaten (V. 19)

TABRISI:92:2-3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:2-3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:2-3/r9.claim: Ibtighāʾ is a causal accusative attached to giving: he gives wealth only to seek his Lord's countenance, not repayment.
TABRISI:92:2-3/r9.anchor: وابتغاء منصوب لأنه مفعول له والعامل فيه يؤتى أي وما يؤتي ماله إلا ابتغاء

TABRISI:92:14-21/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:14-21/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:14-21/r8.claim: He gives solely to seek God's countenance, meaning God Himself, His pleasure, and reward; mentioning the face honors the expression.
TABRISI:92:14-21/r8.anchor: أي ولكنه فعل ما فعل يبتغي به وجه الله ورضاه وثوابه وإنما ذكر الوجه طلبا لشرف الذكر

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r11.claim: He gives solely to seek the pleasure of his Most High Lord.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r11.anchor: Ancak Rabb-i a‘lâsının rızâsını aramak için verir, o ciheti gözetir.

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r14.speaker: Hâkim
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r14.claim: Al-Hakim grades as sound a report from ʿAmir ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father: Abu Quhafa urges Abu Bakr to free strong slaves, but Abu Bakr says he seeks his own purpose, after which the passage is revealed.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r14.anchor: Hâkim, sahih diye Âmir b. Abdullah b. Zübeyr’den, babasından rivayet etmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r1.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r1.claim: Some say verses 19–21 were revealed about Abu Bakr, who bought and freed enslaved people tortured by polytheists.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r3.claim: Polytheists alleged that Abu Bakr freed people in exchange for reciprocal kindness or some benefit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r3.anchor: Müşrikler Hz. Ebû Bekir’in bu yaptıklarını, mukabil bir iyilik veya bir menfaat karşılığında yaptığını iddia etmişlerdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.claim: A pious believer need not receive a favor or gain before helping; all blessings come from God, and good should be done for God's approval alone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r4.anchor: mümin, her türlü nimetin yalnızca Allah’ın bir lutfu olduğuna, iyiliklerin de ilke olarak bir çıkar hesabıyla değil, sadece Allah rızâsı için yapılması gerektiğine inanır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r5.claim: The passage rejects the polytheists' self-interested accusation and honors believers like Abu Bakr, whose hearts are adorned with love for people and generosity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r5.anchor: yukarıdaki iddiaları reddedilmiş, Hz. Ebû Bekir örneğinde gönüllerini insan sevgisi ve cömertlikle bezeyen müminler Allah tarafından takdirle anılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.claim: After warning of the blazing fire in verse 14, verses 17–20 describe giving for God's sake without owing anyone, spiritual purification, and being kept from the fire.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r7.anchor: 14. âyette muhataplar “alev alev yanan ateş”e karşı uyarıldıktan sonra 17-20. âyetlerde, birine borçlu olmadıkları, kimsenin kendilerinde bir hakkı bulunmadığı halde bile

QASHANI:92:19-21/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:19-21/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:19-21/r2.claim: Each divine name has a face through which God discloses Himself to one who calls upon and worships Him with that name’s readiness; the highest face belongs to the all-encompassing Highest name, and the Lord is that name if the phrase is adjectival.
QASHANI:92:19-21/r2.anchor: لأن الله تعالى بحسب كل اسم له وجه يتجلى به لمن يدعوه بلسان حاله بذلك الاسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r6.claim: The exception is disconnected: the giver has no repayable favor, but seeks God's countenance; seeking is a more earnest form of request than baghy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r6.anchor: والاستثناء في { إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه } منقطع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r7.claim: God's face means His essence, so seeking His essence means seeking His approval.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p391/r7.anchor: والوجه مستعمل مرادا به الذات كقوله تعالى : { ويبقى وجه ربك }

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152#4/r1.claim: He gives only to seek the reward of his Lord; al-Farrāʾ takes illā as “rather/only” and understands an omitted “his spending” before seeking.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p152#4/r1.anchor: أي إلا طلبا لثواب ربه قال الفراء و إلا بمعنى لكن ونصب ابتغاء على إضمار إنفاقه

FARRA:v3p273/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p273/r1.claim: Raising ibtighāʾ is acceptable by following the underlying sense of the preceding phrase: no one has a repayable favor except seeking his Lord’s face.
FARRA:v3p273/r1.anchor: ألقيت من: من النعمة لقلت : ما لأحد عنده نعمة تجزى إلا ابتغاء،

FARRA:v3p273/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p273/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p273/r2.claim: A poet’s “a land with no companion except gazelles and white camels” likewise illustrates raising after illā by semantic agreement.
FARRA:v3p273/r2.anchor:
وبلدة ليس بها أنيس ... إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس
فرفع، ولو رفع (إلا

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r1.claim: Mere affirmation is insufficient without piety, contrary to the Murjiʾa; miserliness is blameworthy, and in law means withholding an obligation.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r1.anchor: ومنها: أن البخل مذموم، وذلك في الشرع اسم لمنع الواجب.

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r2.claim: The full set of qualities described earns Paradise and reward.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r6.claim: Ibtigha wajhi rabbihi is an exception from a different class: no one's favor is owed him; he gives only seeking God's face.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r6.anchor: مستثنى من غير جنسه وهو النعمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r7.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r7.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads the exception in the nominative, following a dialect illustrated with poetry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r7.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب : ( إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه ) بالرفع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r8.speaker: بشر بن أبي حازم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r8.claim: Bishr ibn Abi Hazim's line uses an excepted noun with no preceding negative in the nominative, illustrating the dialect cited for this reading.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r8.anchor: قول بشر بن أبي حازم : أضحت خلا فقارا لا أنيس بها … إلا الجآذر والظلمان تختلف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r9.speaker: القائل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r9.claim: An unnamed poet gives a parallel exception construction, illustrating the same dialect.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r9.anchor: وقول القائل : وبلدة ليس بها أنيس … إلا اليعافير وإلا العيس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r10.claim: The phrase may instead be a causal object: he gives only to seek God's face, not to repay a favor.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p768/r10.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { ابتغاء وجه ربه } مفعولا له على المعنى

MAJAZ:v2p301/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p301/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p301/r3.claim: The exception from niʿma is disconnected: it excepts one thing from another of which it is not a part.
MAJAZ:v2p301/r3.anchor: «من نعمة تجزى إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى» (19- 20) استثنى من النعمة كما يستثنى الشيء من الشيء ليس منه.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#4/r1.claim: The benefactor has no debt of favor to anyone that he must repay; he acts only seeking his Lord's face, and God is exalted in authority and proof, not spatially elevated.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p344#4/r1.anchor: أى وما لأحد عند الله نعمة يجازية بها إلا أن يفعل فعلا يبتغى به وجه

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r1.claim: Seeking the Lord’s face means seeking His approval and what brings one near to Him.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r2.claim: Al-aʿla is an epithet of the Lord, who truly possesses attributes of exaltedness.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r2.anchor: و«الأعلى» من نعت الرب الذي استحق صفات العلو

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r3.claim: Ibtighaʾ wajhihi can function as a purpose complement: he gives only to seek God’s approval, not to repay a favor.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون «ابتغاء وجه ربه» مفعولا له على المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r5.speaker: أبو حيان التيمي، علي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan al-Taymi transmits from his father from Ali the Prophet’s praise of Abu Bakr for marrying him to his daughter, carrying him to the migration home, and freeing Bilal.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r5.anchor: وروى أبو حيان التيمي عن أبيه عن علي رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r6.speaker: بلال، أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r6.claim: When Abu Bakr bought Bilal, Bilal asked whether it was for work or God’s sake; Abu Bakr said for God and freed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r6.anchor: ولما اشتراه أبو بكر قال له بلال: هل اشتريتني لعملك أو لعمل الله؟ قال: بل لعمل الله

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r7.claim: Umar called Abu Bakr their master and Bilal the master whom he freed.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r7.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقول: أبو بكر سيدنا وأعتق سيدنا يعني بلالا

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r8.speaker: عطاء، ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r8.claim: A report attributes the sura’s occasion to Abu al-Dahdah buying a palm tree with his orchard, according to al-Thalabi from Ata.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r8.anchor: وقال عطاء وروي عن ابن عباس : إن السورة نزلت في أبي الدحداح في النخلة

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r9.speaker: القشيري، ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r9.claim: Al-Qushayri transmits from Ibn Abbas that the orchard had forty palm trees, without naming the man.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r9.anchor: وقال القشيري عن ابن عباس: بأربعين نخلة ولم يسم الرجل

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r10.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r10.claim: Ata narrates that an Ansari’s overhanging palm dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard, where children ate it; the Prophet offered a Paradise palm, but the owner refused.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r10.anchor: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، يسقط من بلحها في دار جار له، فيتناوله صبيانه

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r11.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r11.claim: Abu al-Dahdah offered his garden called Husna for the tree, then gave it to the Prophet in exchange for a palm in Paradise; the Prophet gave the garden to the neighbor.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r11.anchor: فخرج فلقيه أبو الدحداح فقال: هل لك أن تبيعنيها ب«حسنى»

QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r12.claim: The report concludes that verses through the end of the sura descended concerning Abu al-Dahdah’s orchard and the palm owner.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:20-21/r12.anchor: فنزلت { والليل إذا يغشى } إلى آخر السورة في بستان أبي الدحداح وصاحب النخلة

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r4.claim: The account says Abu al-Dahdah owed no kindness in return and would be satisfied when admitted to Paradise.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r4.anchor: { وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى } يكافئه عليها يعني أبا الدحداح. { ولسوف يرضى } إذا أدخله الله الجنة

QUTB-ZILAL:92:20/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:20/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:20/r1.claim: The God-fearing giver gives wealth to purify himself, not to repay anyone for a favor; his sole motive is seeking his Lord's highest countenance.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:20/r1.anchor: وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى . إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى

QUTB-ZILAL:92:20/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:20/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:20/r2.claim: Qutb builds suspense by asking what this purified, sincere giver awaits, calling the Qur'an's announced reward astonishing, unexpected, and unlike the familiar.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:20/r2.anchor: إن الجزاء الذي يطالع القرآن به الأرواح المؤمنة هنا عجيب . ومفاجئ . وعلى غير المألوف

RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r6.claim: A report says Bilal, enslaved by ʿAbd Allah ibn Judʿan, was sold to polytheists with camels after complaints about his treatment of idols; they tortured him in the heat as he repeated 'One, One.'
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r6.anchor: كان بلال ( عبدا ) لعبد الله بن جدعان

RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r7.claim: The Prophet told Bilal God would save him, then informed Abu Bakr of the torture; Abu Bakr bought him with gold, and the claim that Bilal owed him a favor prompted the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v31p185#2/r7.anchor: ثم أخبر رسول الله أبا بكر أن بلالا يعذب في الله

RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r1.claim: One parse treats seeking the Lord's face as an exception unlike the preceding favor: he owes nobody a favor and only seeks God's face.
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r1.anchor: ابتغاء وجه ربه } مستثنى من غير جنسه وهو النعمة

RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r2.claim: Al-Farra supplies an implied verb of spending: he spends only to seek his Lord's face, as in 2:272.
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r2.anchor: وذكر الفراء فيه وجها آخر وهو أن يضمر الإنفاق

RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.claim: The pious giver is not repaying an earlier gift or favor, which would merely settle a debt; reward is due because he gives in response to God's command.
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r3.anchor: لا يؤتيه مكافأة على هدية أو نعمة سالفة

RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r4.claim: Anthropomorphists appeal to 'face' and deniers to 'his highest Lord' as implying another lord; Razi says these issues were discussed earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r4.anchor: المجسمة تمسكوا بلفظة الوجه والملحدة تمسكوا بلفظة

RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r5.claim: Al-Baqillani contrasts Ali's feeding verse, motivated by God's face and fear of Judgment, with Abu Bakr's verse, which he reads as pure devotion without hope of reward or fear of punishment; he ranks Abu Bakr higher.
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r5.anchor: ذكر القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني في كتاب الإمامة

RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r6.claim: Some say seeking God means seeking His reward and honor because seeking His essence is impossible; others affirm love of God Himself, a question discussed at 2:165.
RAZI-FULL:v31p186#2/r6.anchor: من الناس من قال : ابتغاء الله بمعنى ابتغاء ذاته وهي محال

RAZI-FULL:v31p187/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p187/r1.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
RAZI-FULL:v31p187/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads seeking the Lord's face in the nominative, supported by a dialect that raises an exception, as in the cited poem.
RAZI-FULL:v31p187/r1.anchor: قرأ يحيى بن وثاب : { إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه } بالرفع

SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats ibtighāʾa as a purpose object by sense: wealth is given seeking God's approval, not repayment for a favor.
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مفعولا له على المعنى؛ لأن المعنى: لا يؤتي ماله إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه

SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r2.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ similarly paraphrases: I gave not to seek your reward but to seek God's approval.
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r2.anchor: ما أعطيتك ابتغاء جزائك، بل ابتغاء وجه الله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r3.claim: Alternatively, the accusative is a disconnected exception because seeking God's face is outside the class of favors received; this is the common reading.
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r3.anchor: أنه منصوب على الاستثناء المنقطع، إذ لم يندرج تحت جنس " من نعمة " وهذه قراءة العامة

SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r4.speaker: يحيى
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r4.claim: Yaḥyā reads ibtighāʾu in the nominative as an appositive to the syntactically nominative min niʿmah; this follows the Tamimi usage of disconnected exceptions in nonaffirmative clauses.
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r4.anchor: وقرأ يحيى برفعه ممدودا على البدل من محل " من نعمة

SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī cites poetry from Bishr ibn Abī Khāzim for the accusative and a second poet for a raised exception.
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r5.anchor: وأنشد الزمخشري بالوجهين: النصب والبدل قول بشر بن أبي خازم

SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r6.speaker: مكي
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r6.claim: Makkī calls the nominative apposition reading distant; the author replies that he seems unaware it is transmitted and that it is a widespread dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r6.anchor: وقال مكي: " وأجاز الفراء الرفع في " ابتغاء " على البدل من موضع " نعمة " وهو بعيد

SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r7.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r7.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads ibtighāʾ with a shortened final vowel.
SAMIN-DURR:92:20/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن ابي عبلة " ابتغا " بالقصر.

TAB:92:19/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:19/r1.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:19/r1.claim: A grammarian reads the clause as denying that the giver owes any creature repayment for a favor; he gives for God's sake alone.
TAB:92:19/r1.anchor: وما لأحد من خلق الله عند هذا الذي يؤتى ماله في سبيل الله يتزكى مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزَى يعني :  من يد يكافئه عليها

TAB:92:19/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:19/r2.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:19/r2.claim: On this reading, illa means ‘but’; repayment may be future, and the giver seeks no person's recompense for his spending.
TAB:92:19/r2.anchor: قال :  وإلا في هذا الموضع بمعنى لكن وقال :  يجوز أن يكون الفعل في المكافأة مستقبلاً

TAB:92:19/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:19/r5.speaker: author
TAB:92:19/r5.claim: Al-Tabari endorses the grammarian's repayment-free reading as correct because reports from the early interpreters support it.
TAB:92:19/r5.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله الذي حكينا قوله من أهل العربية ،   وزعم أنه مما يجوز هو الصحيح

TAB:92:19/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:19/r6.speaker: author
TAB:92:19/r6.claim: On that interpretation, ‘seeking his Lord's face’ is an accusative exception from the implied motive of the spending; it can also be accusative by contrast with what follows illa.
TAB:92:19/r6.anchor: ينبغي أن يكون قوله :  إلاّ ابْتِغَآءَ وَجْهِ رَبّهِ الأعْلَى نصبا على الاستثناء من معنى قوله

TAB:92:19/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:19/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:19/r7.claim: Qatada says the verse concerns Abu Bakr: he seeks no reward or repayment from people, only God's approval.
TAB:92:19/r7.anchor: عن قتادة وَما لاِءَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزَى إلاّ ابْتِغاءَ وَجْهِ رَبّهِ الأعْلَى

TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r1.claim: The giver spends neither to repay anyone for a favor nor to earn repayment; he gives for God's sake alone.
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى ولسوف يرضى} [الليل: 20] يقول: ليس به مثابة الناس ولا مجازاتهم

TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r2.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r2.claim: Some grammarians take illā here as 'but' and allow either an understood future repayment or a shifted preposition construction.
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r2.anchor: وإلا في هذا الموضع بمعنى لكن؛ وقال: يجوز أن يكون الفعل في المكافأة مستقبلا

TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says this man does not give to be repaid or thanked by people; he gives only for God.
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى ولسوف يرضى} [الليل: 20] يقول: ليس به مثابة الناس

TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r4.speaker: ابن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r4.claim: A report from ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh's father says the verse was revealed about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r4.anchor: عن عامر بن عبد الله، عن أبيه، قال: نزلت هذه الآية في أبي بكر الصديق

TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says the verse concerned Abū Bakr freeing six or seven people, including Bilāl and ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra, without seeking reward or thanks.
TAB-FULL:v24p478#2/r5.anchor: قال: نزلت في أبي بكر، أعتق ناسا لم يلتمس منهم جزاء ولا شكورا، ستة أو سبعة، منهم بلال

TAB-FULL:v24p480/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p480/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p480/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites al-Nābigha's lines as evidence for the Arabic construction discussed in interpreting the exception in this verse.
TAB-FULL:v24p480/r1.anchor: وقفت فيها أصيلانا أسائلها … عيت جوابا وما بالربع من أحد

TABATABAI:92:20-21/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r2.claim: The exception is disconnected: he gives his wealth only while seeking the face of his Most High Lord.
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r2.anchor: استثناء منقطع والمعنى ولكنه يؤتي ماله طلبا لوجه ربه الأعلى

TABATABAI:92:20-21/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:20-21/r5.claim: The phrase ‘his Most High Lord’ makes a rhetorical shift from first-person speech to third-person reference through the two divine attributes.

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r5.claim: Abū al-Daḥdāḥ is the God-fearing person kept away from the Fire because he gives his wealth to purify himself, seeking only his Lord’s face rather than repaying a favor.
THALABI:v10p220/r5.anchor: وسيجنبها الأتقى يعني أبا الدحداح الذي يؤتي ماله يتزكى يعني أبا الدحداح وما لأحد عنده من نعمة تجزى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r1.claim: Seeking God's face means seeking God's reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r1.anchor: {إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى} (أي إلا طلب ثواب الله)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r2.claim: The exception is syntactically from “favor,” though an exception can be something outside the category, as in ordinary Arabic usage and 4:157.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: "إلا ابتغاء" (¬5) استثناء من النعمة، كما يستثنى الشيء وليس منه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r3.claim: The construction contrasts what precedes and follows the exception, like the poetic example and 4:157; al-Farrāʾ calls this Hijazi usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: وهذا على اختلاف ما قبل "إلا" وما بعدها، والعرب تقول: ما في الدار أحد إلا أكلبا وأحمرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r4.speaker: النابغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r4.claim: The poet's verse illustrates an exception of something outside the preceding category.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r4.anchor: كقول (¬7) النابغة: .. .. وما بالربع من أحد # إلا الأواري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r5.claim: Alternatively, supply “spending”: he spends only to seek God's face, as in 2:272.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r5.anchor: وذكر الفراء وجها آخر، وهو: أن يضمر الإنفاق على تقدير: ما ينفق إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r6.claim: Al-aʿlā means supremely exalted in incomparable attributes: the most powerful, dominant, and manifest through proof and might.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p90/r6.anchor: ومعنى {الأعلى}: الأجل بصفاته التي لا يوارى فيها، فهو الأقدر

WAHIDI-QT:92:20/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:20/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:20/r1.claim: He acts only to seek his Lord's reward.
WAHIDI-QT:92:20/r1.anchor: { إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى } أي لكن طلب ثواب الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:20-21/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:20-21/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:20-21/r1.claim: Seeking the face of the Most High means seeking God's reward.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:20:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:20:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:20:anmerkung/r1.claim: Seeking God’s face is a biblical motif: compare 76:9 and Psalms 27:8 and 105:4, 2 Samuel 21:1, and Hosea 5:15.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:20:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Die Wendung ist, wie Baljon 1953 gezeigt hat, ein biblischer Topos

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p456/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p456/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p456/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after Bilal defiled idols, his owner gave him to the polytheists, who tortured him; Abu Bakr bought his freedom with gold, but they alleged a prior debt, so the verses affirmed he acted only seeking God's face.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p456/r1.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: إن بلالا لما أسلم ذهب إلى الأصنام فسلح عليها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r1.claim: The exception is disconnected because seeking God's pleasure is not a favor: he gives to seek divine approval, not to repay anyone. The phrase may also be a purpose-object or an exception from all possible motives, understood from the context's denial of ostentation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r1.anchor: منصوب على الأستثناء المنقطع من نعمة لأن الأبتغاء لا يندرج فيها فالمعنى لكنهفعل ذلك لابتغاء وجه ربه سبحانه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r2.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r2.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads ابتغاء in the nominative as a substitute for the syntactic position of من نعمة; this nominative construction is a Tamīm dialect, supported by poetry.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب ابتغاء بالرفع على البدل من محل من نعمة فإنه الرفع إما على الفاعلية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r3.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads the shortened form ابتغاء, which permits either nominative or accusative parsing.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة إلا ابتغاء مقصور وفيه احتمال النصب والرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r4.claim: The passage concerns Abū Bakr, who freed vulnerable enslaved people; a report says his father challenged the expense, and he answered that he sought God's reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r4.anchor: وهذه الآيات على ما سمعتنزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه لما أنه كان يعتق رقابا ضعافا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r5.claim: A report from ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk says Abū Bakr bought and freed Bilāl, tortured for Islam, and pagans claimed he owed him a favor; the verse was revealed in response.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r5.anchor: وفي رواية عطاء والضحاك عن ابن عباسأنه رضي الله تعالى عنه اشترى بلالا وكان رقيقا لأمية ابن خلف يعذبه لأسلامه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r6.speaker: عروة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r6.claim: ʿUrwa reports that Abū Bakr freed seven people being tortured for God: Bilāl, ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra, al-Nahdiyya and her daughter, Dhanīra, Umm ʿUbays, and a slave woman of Banū al-Muʾammal.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r6.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عروة أن أبا بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه أعتق سبعة كلهم يعذب في الله عز وجل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r7.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r7.claim: The Imam uses these verses to argue that Abū Bakr was the community's best, and says their context rules out the Shīʿī claim that they concern ʿAlī; Alusi notes that the argument is lengthy and disputable.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p152#2/r7.anchor: واستدل بذلك الإمام على أنه رضي الله تعالى عنه أفضل الأمة وذكر أن في الآيات ما يأبى قول الشيعة أنها في علي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p449#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p449#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p449#2/r2.claim: He acts to seek the Most High Lord's face and favor, not to repay anyone for a favor owed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p449#2/r2.anchor: لا يفعل ذلك مجازاة لأحد بيد له عنده، ولكنه يفعله ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى وطلب رضاه

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r1.claim: The exception may be disconnected, or connected to an omitted clause meaning that he gives only to seek God's countenance, not to repay a favor.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r1.anchor: استثناء منقطع أو متصل عن محذوف مثل لا يؤتى إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r3.claim: These verses were revealed concerning Abū Bakr, who bought and freed Bilāl and other people persecuted by polytheists; the wretched person is consequently identified as Abū Jahl or Umayya ibn Khalaf.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r3.anchor: والآيات نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه حين اشترى بلالا في جماعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r4.claim: A report promises enough provision to satisfy the reciter and relief from hardship with an easy path.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:20-21/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة والليل أعطاه الله سبحانه وتعالى حتى يرضى

BINTSHATI:v2p118/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r4.speaker: الجمهور
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r4.claim: The majority read ibtighāʾ in the accusative.
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r4.anchor: القراءة بنصب ابتغاء، هي قراءة الجمهور.

BINTSHATI:v2p118/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r5.speaker: الفراء والزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r5.claim: They allow the accusative as an object of purpose, alongside its analysis as an exception; Quranic usage commonly puts this form in the accusative as an object of purpose.
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r5.anchor: مفعولاً لأجله كما ذهب "الفراء" و"الزمخشري" في الكشاف.

BINTSHATI:v2p118/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r6.speaker: البحر المحيط
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r6.claim: The raised reading is interpreted as a nominative substitute for niʿma, with a redundant preposition before it.
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r6.anchor: فتأولوه فيها على البدل من نعمة، وهي من الصنعة الإعرابية في موضع رفع، وحرف الجر قبلها زائد (البحر المحيط)

BINTSHATI:v2p118/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r7.claim: Ibtighāʾ means seeking a desired end with exertion; in negative contexts it carries overtones of aggression and exceeding limits, while in good contexts it conveys diligent pursuit.
BINTSHATI:v2p118/r7.anchor: الإبتغاء في اللغة، التماس بغية يجتهد في طلبها.

BINTSHATI:v2p119/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r1.claim: The author sets aside theological disputes about the divine “face” to focus on its linguistic and rhetorical use.
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r1.anchor: ولا مجال للخوض هنا فيما تعلق به المجسمة من لفظ "وجه" وما حلفت به كتب الكلاميين من تأويل له

BINTSHATI:v2p119/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r2.claim: Wajh literally denotes the part of something that faces you, most often the bodily face, as in the examples about Joseph and Abraham's wife.
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r2.anchor: الوجه في اللغة ما يستقبلك من كل شيء، وأكثر ما يستعمل حسياً للوجه المعروف من الجسم

BINTSHATI:v2p119/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r3.claim: Arabic also uses “face” for a person's self because it distinguishes and identifies that person, and by extension for the notable people themselves.
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r3.anchor: والعربية تطلق الوجه، مراداً به الذات، من حيث كان الوجه هو الذي يميز الشخص ويحدد ملامحه.

BINTSHATI:v2p119/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r4.claim: Because the face is the body's foremost facing part, wajh can also mean aim or direction.
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r4.anchor: وبملحظ من كون الوجه هو أول ما يستقبل الجسم، جاء الوجه بمعنى القصد والإتجاه.

BINTSHATI:v2p119/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p119/r5.claim: The author illustrates the physical sense of face with Qur'anic uses for washing, wiping, and turning faces toward the qibla.

BINTSHATI:v2p120/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r1.claim: Of eleven Qur'anic occurrences of “God's face,” eight concern spending or worship directed toward God.
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r1.anchor: وقد جاء "وجه" مضافاً إلى الله سبحانه في إحدى عشرة آية من القرآن الكريم

BINTSHATI:v2p120/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r2.claim: One interpretation treats “face” as an expendable word meaning simply God; others reject that and take it as purpose and orientation.
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r2.anchor: قيل في تأويلها إن لفظ وجه "في كل هذا زائد، والمعنى: فثم الله، كل شيء هالك إلا هو

BINTSHATI:v2p120/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r3.claim: The author favors the established Arabic idiom in which face can denote the self, as in “the face of truth” or “the face of the matter,” without implying embodiment.
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r3.anchor: ونقتصر هنا في التفسير البياني، على ما ألفته العربية في إطلاقها الوجه مقصوداً به الذات

BINTSHATI:v2p120/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r4.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī notes that opponents infer from “his Lord, the Most High” that another, lower lord must exist.
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r4.anchor: وأشار الرازي في تفسيره إلى ما يتعلق به الملحدة في "ربه الأعلى"

BINTSHATI:v2p120/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r5.claim: The author rejects that inference: al-aʿlā is an unbounded superlative carrying elevation to its furthest extent, not comparison with a lesser god; the same holds for al-Aʿlā 1.
BINTSHATI:v2p120/r5.anchor: وإنما القصد إلى المضي بالعلو إلى نهايته القصوى

ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r1.claim: The majority read ibtighāʾ in the accusative as a disconnected exception, since it is not included among the favors.
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r1.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { إلا ابتغاء } بنصب الهمزة ،   وهو استثناء منقطع

ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r2.speaker: ابن وثاب
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r2.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads in the nominative as an apposition to niʿmah, also nominative, following Tamīm usage; poetry is cited for both case forms.
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب : بالرفع على البدل في موضع نعمة

ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r3.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r3.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAblah reads the word in a shortened form without hamza.
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة : { إلا ابتغاء } ،   مقصوراً

ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows ibtighāʾ to be an object of purpose by sense: he gives wealth to seek his Lord's face, not to repay favors.
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : ويجوز أن يكون ابتغاء وجه الله مفعولاً له

ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r5.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ gives the same semantic analysis: wealth is not given for recompense but to seek God's face.
ABUHAYYAN:92:20/r5.anchor: قال الفراء : ونصب على تأويل ما أعطيك ابتغاء جزائك

ALUSI:92:20/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:20/r1.claim: The accusative ابتغاء is a disconnected exception from نعمة, since seeking God’s face is not itself a favor; the meaning is that he acts to seek God’s pleasure, not to repay a favor.
ALUSI:92:20/r1.anchor: منصوب على الاستثناء المنقطع من { نعمة } لأن الابتغاء لا يندرج فيها

ALUSI:92:20/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:20/r2.claim: Seeking the Lord’s face means seeking His approval, rather than recompensing someone for a favor.
ALUSI:92:20/r2.anchor: وطلب رضاه عز وجل لا لمكافأة نعمة

ALUSI:92:20/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r3.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
ALUSI:92:20/r3.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads ابتغاء in the nominative, apposed to the grammatical position of من نعمة; من is extra, and the nominative may be subject or topic.
ALUSI:92:20/r3.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب ابتغاء بالرفع على البدل من محل من نعمة فإنه الرفع إما على الفاعلية أو على الابتداء ومن مزيدة

ALUSI:92:20/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:20/r4.claim: The nominative after this kind of إلا is a Tamīm dialect, illustrated by a line about a land with no people except gazelles and camels.
ALUSI:92:20/r4.anchor: والرفع في مثل ذلك لغة تميم وعليها قوله

ALUSI:92:20/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r5.speaker: بشر بن أبي حازم
ALUSI:92:20/r5.claim: Al-Baḥr cites a line by Bishr ibn Abī Ḥāzim transmitted with either nominative or accusative after إلا.
ALUSI:92:20/r5.anchor: وروي بالرفع والنصب على ما في البحر قول بشر بن أبي حازم

ALUSI:92:20/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:20/r6.claim: Another parse makes the accusative a purpose complement by sense, as a free exception from all causes: he gives wealth for no reason except seeking his Lord’s approval.
ALUSI:92:20/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يكون نصبه على أنه مفعول له على المعنى لأن معنى الكلام لا يؤتي ماله لأجل شيء من الأشياء إلا لأجل طلب رضا ربه

ALUSI:92:20/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:20/r7.claim: Though a free exception is normally restricted to negative clauses, the following denial that anyone has a favor to repay and the earlier تزكى imply the needed negation and exclude ostentation.

ALUSI:92:20/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r8.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI:92:20/r8.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads ابتغا with a shortened final vowel, permitting either the accusative or nominative parse.
ALUSI:92:20/r8.anchor: وقرأ بن أبي عبلة إلا ابتغا مقصور وفيه احتمال النصب والرفع

ALUSI:92:20/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:20/r9.claim: The passage is said to have been revealed about Abū Bakr, who freed weak enslaved believers; when his father questioned him, he answered that he sought God’s reward.
ALUSI:92:20/r9.anchor: هذه الآيات على ما سمعت نزلت في أبي بكر رضي الله تعالى عنه لما أنه كان يعتق رقاباً ضعافاً فقال له أبوه

ALUSI:92:20/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r10.speaker: أبو بكر
ALUSI:92:20/r10.claim: A version transmitted by Ibn Jarīr and Ibn ʿAsākir gives Abū Bakr’s reply to his father: he sought only what is with God.
ALUSI:92:20/r10.anchor: وفي رواية ابن جرير وابن عساكر أنه قال أي أبه إنما أريد ما عند الله تعالى

ALUSI:92:20/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI:92:20/r11.claim: In a report from Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Abū Bakr bought the tortured Bilāl from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a weight of gold and freed him; the polytheists claimed he repaid a favor.
ALUSI:92:20/r11.anchor: وفي رواية عطاء والضحاك عن ابن عباس أنه رضي الله تعالى عنه اشترى بلالاً وكان رقيقاً لأمية بن خلف يعذبه لإسلامه برطل من ذهب

ALUSI:92:20/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r12.speaker: عروة
ALUSI:92:20/r12.claim: ʿUrwa reports that Abū Bakr freed seven people tortured for God’s sake: Bilāl, ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra, al-Nahdiyya and her daughter, Dīnara, Umm ʿĪsā and a slave woman of Banū al-Muʾammil.
ALUSI:92:20/r12.anchor: فقد أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عروة أن أبا بكر الصديق رضي الله تعالى عنه أعتق سبعة كلهم يعذب في الله

ALUSI:92:20/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:20/r13.claim: Al-Ālūsī adds that Abū Bakr himself had been tortured for his faith, and al-Ṣiddīq bought and freed such people; verse 17 through the end of the sūra was revealed about him.
ALUSI:92:20/r13.anchor: وهو رضي الله تعالى عنه أحد الذين عذبوا لإسلامهم فاشتراهم الصديق وأعتقهم فقد أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عروة

ALUSI:92:20/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:20/r14.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI:92:20/r14.claim: Al-Imām uses the passage as evidence that Abū Bakr was the community’s most excellent member and argues that its context weighs against the Shīʿī claim that it concerns ʿAlī; al-Ālūsī notes the debate is not free of disputation.
ALUSI:92:20/r14.anchor: واستدل بذلك الإمام علي أنه رضي الله تعالى عنه أفضل الأمة وذكر أن في الآيات ما يأبى قول الشيعة أنها في علي

BAGHAWI:92:20/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:20/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:20/r1.claim: He acts neither to repay a favor owed to anyone nor for a person's benefit, but seeks his Most High Lord's face and pleasure.
BAGHAWI:92:20/r1.anchor: لا يفعل ذلك مجازاة لأحد بيد له عنده ، ولكنه يفعله ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى وطلب رضاه

BAYDAWI:92:20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:20/r1.claim: The exception may be disconnected, or connected to an omitted phrase such as “he gives only seeking his Lord's face.”
BAYDAWI:92:20/r1.anchor: إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه الأعلى استثناء منقطع أو متصل عن محذوف مثل لا يؤتى إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه

BAYDAWI:92:20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:20/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:20/r2.claim: The giving seeks the Lord's face, not repayment for a favor.

BIQAI:92:20/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:20/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:20/r1.claim: The exception is disconnected: the giver's aim is not repayment, but seeking God's pleasure.
BIQAI:92:20/r1.anchor: قال مبيناً قصده باستثناء منقطع : { إلا } أي لكن قصد بذلك { ابتغاء } أي طلب وقصد ،

BIQAI:92:20/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:20/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:20/r2.claim: The Lord is the benefactor who created and nurtured him; the giver sees no beneficence except God's and possesses nothing but God's grace. God's Face names the highest aim, His own essence, rather than any worldly or afterlife reward.
BIQAI:92:20/r2.anchor: الذي أوجده ورباه وأحسن إليه بحيث إنه لم ير إحساناً إلا منه ولا عنده شيء إلا وهو من فضله

BIQAI:92:20/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:20/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:20/r3.claim: Calling God absolutely Most High means no one can give anything from himself that could repay God; using the connected exception particle for this disconnected exception makes seeking God's pleasure seem itself a divine gift that prompted the donation.
BIQAI:92:20/r3.anchor: وعبر عن المنقطع بأداة المتصل للإشارة إلى أن الابتغاء المذكور كأنه نعمة ممن آتاه المال

IBNASHUR:92:20/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:20/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:20/r1.claim: The negative ma is governed by an extra min that strengthens negation; the exception is disconnected and means but seeking God's face.
IBNASHUR:92:20/r1.anchor: اسم { ما } النافية جر ب { من } الزائدة التي تزاد في النفي

IBNASHUR:92:20/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:20/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:20/r2.claim: Ibtigha is earnest seeking, stronger in force than baghy.
IBNASHUR:92:20/r2.anchor: والابتغاء :  الطلب بجد لأنه أبلغ من البغي

IBNASHUR:92:20/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:20/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:20/r3.claim: Face denotes God's essence; seeking His essence means seeking His approval.
IBNASHUR:92:20/r3.anchor: والوجه مستعمل مراداً به الذات كقوله تعالى :  { ويبقى وجه ربك }

IBNATIYYA:92:20/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:20/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:20/r1.claim: His giving is not repayment for a favor previously received; he gives spontaneously, seeking God's approval.
IBNATIYYA:92:20/r1.anchor: معناه : وليس إعطاؤه ليجزي نعما قد أنزلت إليه بل هو مبتدئ ابتغاء وجه الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:92:20/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:20/r2.speaker: قريش
IBNATIYYA:92:20/r2.claim: When Abū Bakr freed Bilāl, Quraysh alleged that Bilāl had previously done Abū Bakr a favor.
IBNATIYYA:92:20/r2.anchor: وروي في سبب هذا أن قريشا قالوا -لما أعتق أبو بكر رضي الله عنه بلالا- : كانت لبلال يد عنده

IBNATIYYA:92:20/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:20/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:20/r5.claim: Ibtighāʾ is parsed as an exception disconnected from the preceding construction; the word means seeking.
IBNATIYYA:92:20/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى [ إلا ابتغاء ] نصب بالاستثناء المنقطع وفيه نظر ، والابتغاء : الطلب

IBNKATHIR:92:20/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:20/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:92:20/r1.claim: The righteous giver is moved by hope of seeing his Most High Lord in the Hereafter, in the gardens of Paradise.
IBNKATHIR:92:20/r1.anchor: أي : طمعًا في أن يحصل له رؤيته في الدار الآخرة في روضات الجنات ،

KASHSHAF:92:20/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:20/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:20/r1.claim: The exception is of a different category from the favor: no one has a favor owed to him, since his giving is only to seek his Lord’s face; this resembles saying “no one is in the house except a donkey.”
KASHSHAF:92:20/r1.anchor: { ابتغاء وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ } مستثنى من غير جنسه وهو النعمة أي : ما لأحد عنده نعمة إلاّ ابتغاء وجه ربه ،

KASHSHAF:92:20/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:20/r2.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
KASHSHAF:92:20/r2.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads “ibtighāʾu” in the nominative, following the dialect that says “there is no one in the house except a donkey.”
KASHSHAF:92:20/r2.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب : «إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه » بالرفع : على لغة من يقول : ما في الدار أحد ألا حمار

KASHSHAF:92:20/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:20/r3.speaker: بشر بن أبي حازم
KASHSHAF:92:20/r3.claim: Bishr ibn Abī Ḥāzim’s verse and a second, anonymous line witness the two exception constructions after negation.
KASHSHAF:92:20/r3.anchor: وأنشد في اللغتين قول بشر بن أبي حازم : أَضْحَتْ خَلاءً قِفَاراً لاَ أَنِيسَ بِهَا

KASHSHAF:92:20/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:20/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:20/r4.claim: The phrase may instead be a purpose complement: he gives his wealth only to seek his Lord’s face, not to repay a favor.
KASHSHAF:92:20/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { ابتغاء وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ } مفعولاً له على المعنى ، لأنّ معنى الكلام : لا يؤتي ماله إلاّ ابتغاء وجه ربه ، لا لمكافأة نعمة .

MAWARDI:92:20/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:20/r1.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI:92:20/r1.claim: No one has a favor against a person to repay; rather, the person acts seeking God’s face and thereby deserves reward from Him.
MAWARDI:92:20/r1.anchor: أحدهما : وما لأحد عند الله تعالى من نعمة يجازيه بها إلا أن يفعلها ابتغاء وجه ربه فيستحق عليها الجزاء والثواب ، قاله قتادة

MAWARDI:92:20/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:20/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
MAWARDI:92:20/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Masʿūd apply this to Abū Bakr: he freed Bilāl from slavery and torment without a prior favor to repay, seeking only God’s face.
MAWARDI:92:20/r2.anchor: حين اشتراه فأعتقه من الرق وخلصه من العذاب نعمة سلفت جازاه عليها بذلك إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه وعتقه ، قاله ابن عباس وابن مسعود

NASAFI:92:20/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:20/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:20/r1.claim: No one has a favor with God that needs repaying; rather a person acts seeking God's face, and God rewards that deed.
NASAFI:92:20/r1.anchor: أي وما لأحد عند الله نعمة يجازيه بها إلا أن يفعل فعلا يبتغي به وجه ربه فيجازيه عليه

NASAFI:92:20/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:20/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:20/r2.claim: “The Most High” means exalted in dominion and inaccessible in status and proof, not spatial height, which would imply createdness.
NASAFI:92:20/r2.anchor: هو الرفيع بسلطانه المنيع في شأنه وبرهانه ، ولم يرد به العلو من حيث المكان

QURTUBI:92:20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r1.claim: He gives without seeking repayment for anyone's favor; he seeks his transcendent Lord's good pleasure, and will be satisfied by the recompense.
QURTUBI:92:20/r1.anchor: أي ليس يتصدق ليجازي على نعمة ، إنما يبتغي وجه ربه الأعلى ، أي المتعالي

QURTUBI:92:20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI:92:20/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk report from Ibn ʿAbbās that persecuted Bilāl cried One, One; the Prophet promised God would save him and alerted Abū Bakr, who bought and freed him, prompting the charge that Abū Bakr repaid a favor and this verse's revelation.
QURTUBI:92:20/r2.anchor: فروى عطاء والضحاك عن ابن عباس قال : عذب المشركون بلالا ، وبلال يقول أحد أحد

QURTUBI:92:20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r3.claim: Another account says Abū Bakr bought Bilāl from Umayya and Ubayy ibn Khalaf for a cloak and ten uqiyyas and freed him for God; it associates the revelation with 92:4.
QURTUBI:92:20/r3.anchor: وقيل : اشترى أبو بكر من أمية وأبي بن خلف بلالا ، ببردة وعشر أواق ، فأعتقه لله

QURTUBI:92:20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI:92:20/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib reports that Umayya offered Bilāl for Nustās, Abū Bakr's wealthy polytheist slave; Abū Bakr offered to make Nustās Muslim and transfer his property, but he refused, so Abū Bakr exchanged him for Bilāl, leading the polytheists to allege a debt to Bilāl.
QURTUBI:92:20/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب : بلغني أن أمية بن خلف قال لأبي بكر حين قال له أبو بكر : أتبيعنيه ؟

QURTUBI:92:20/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r5.claim: The exception is disconnected, meaning but seeking God's face, so it is accusative; he illustrates this with no one in the house except a donkey, while nominative is also possible.
QURTUBI:92:20/r5.anchor: فهو استثناء منقطع ؛ فلذلك نصبت . كقولك : ما في الدار أحد إلا حمارا . ويجوز الرفع

QURTUBI:92:20/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r6.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
QURTUBI:92:20/r6.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads ابتغاء in the nominative, reflecting the dialect that permits a nominative after إلا; poetry and 4:66 illustrate this usage.
QURTUBI:92:20/r6.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب " إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه " بالرفع ، على لغة من يقول : يجوز الرفع في المستثنى

QURTUBI:92:20/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r7.claim: Face of the Lord means His approval and what draws one near Him; al-Aʿlā describes the Lord, who possesses the attributes of exaltedness.
QURTUBI:92:20/r7.anchor: من نعت الرب الذي استحق صفات العلو

QURTUBI:92:20/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r8.claim: By the sense of the sentence, seeking the Lord's face can be a purpose complement: he gives wealth only to seek God's face, not to repay a favor.
QURTUBI:92:20/r8.anchor: مفعولا له على المعنى ؛ لأن معنى الكلام : لا يؤتي ماله إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه

QURTUBI:92:20/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r9.claim: He will receive in Paradise what pleases him, with a reward many times greater than what he spent.
QURTUBI:92:20/r9.anchor: أي سوف يعطيه في الجنة ما يرضي ، وذلك أنه يعطيه أضعاف ما أنفق

QURTUBI:92:20/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r10.speaker: علي
QURTUBI:92:20/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān al-Taymī transmits from his father, from ʿAlī, the Prophet's prayer for Abū Bakr, who married him to his daughter, carried him to the migration home, and freed Bilāl from his wealth.
QURTUBI:92:20/r10.anchor: وروى أبو حيان التيمي عن أبيه عن علي رضي الله عنه ، قال : قال رسول الله

QURTUBI:92:20/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r11.speaker: بلال
QURTUBI:92:20/r11.claim: When Abū Bakr bought him, Bilāl asked whether he had been bought for service or for God's cause; Abū Bakr said God's cause, and freed him.
QURTUBI:92:20/r11.anchor: ولما اشتراه أبو بكر قال له بلال : هل اشتريتني لعملك أو لعمل الله

QURTUBI:92:20/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r12.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
QURTUBI:92:20/r12.claim: ʿUmar called Abū Bakr their master and Bilāl the master whom Abū Bakr freed.
QURTUBI:92:20/r12.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقول : أبو بكر سيدنا وأعتق سيدنا يعني بلالا

QURTUBI:92:20/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r13.speaker: عطاء وابن عباس
QURTUBI:92:20/r13.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, with a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, says the sūra came down about Abū al-Daḥdāḥ and the palm he bought with his orchard; al-Qushayrī says Ibn ʿAbbās specified forty palms but did not name the man.
QURTUBI:92:20/r13.anchor: وقال عطاء - وروى عن ابن عباس - : إن السورة نزلت في أبي الدحداح ، في النخلة

QURTUBI:92:20/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r14.claim: An Anṣārī's palm dropped dates into a neighbor's home, where children took them; after the Prophet's offer of a palm in Paradise was refused, Abū al-Daḥdāḥ traded his orchard for it and gave the palm to the neighbor, and the sūra was revealed about them.
QURTUBI:92:20/r14.anchor: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة ، يسقط من بلحها في دار جار له ، فيتناول صبيانه

QURTUBI:92:20/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:20/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:20/r18.claim: The one spending to purify himself is Abū al-Daḥdāḥ paying for the palm; he owed nobody a favor to repay, and acted only for God's sake.

RAZI:92:20/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:20/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:20/r1.claim: Rāzī reads seeking the Lord's face as an exception from a different category than the favor or benefit owed to the giver, like saying there is nobody in the house except a donkey.
RAZI:92:20/r1.anchor: مستثنى من غير جنسه وهو النعمة

RAZI:92:20/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:20/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:92:20/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ offers an alternative ellipsis: understand that the spending is only for seeking God's face, as in 2:272.

RAZI:92:20/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:20/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:92:20/r3.claim: The pious giver is not repaying a prior gift or favor, which would merely discharge a debt; reward is earned by giving because God commanded and urged it.
RAZI:92:20/r3.anchor: لأن ذلك يجري مجرى أداء الدين

RAZI:92:20/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:20/r4.speaker: المجسمة
RAZI:92:20/r4.claim: The anthropomorphists appeal to the word face in the verse.

RAZI:92:20/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:20/r5.speaker: الملحدة
RAZI:92:20/r5.claim: The atheists appeal to the phrase his Lord the Most High as though it entailed another lord.

RAZI:92:20/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:20/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
RAZI:92:20/r6.claim: In al-Imāma, al-Bāqillānī assigns the feeding-for-God verses to ʿAlī and this verse to Abū Bakr; both acted for God, but ʿAlī also feared Judgment, so Abū Bakr's station is higher.
RAZI:92:20/r6.anchor: ذكر القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني في كتاب

RAZI:92:20/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:20/r7.speaker: من الناس
RAZI:92:20/r7.claim: One view says seeking God means seeking His essence, which is impossible, so the phrase must mean seeking His reward and honor.
RAZI:92:20/r7.anchor: من الناس من قال : ابتغاء الله بمعنى

RAZI:92:20/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:20/r8.speaker: من الناس
RAZI:92:20/r8.claim: Another view sees no need for an ellipsis; the underlying dispute is whether a servant can love God's essence or only His reward and honor, discussed under 2:165.
RAZI:92:20/r8.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : لا حاجة إلى هذا الإضمار

RAZI:92:20/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:20/r9.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
RAZI:92:20/r9.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads ibtighāʾ in the nominative, following a dialect that makes the exception nominative after a negative; the cited verse line illustrates the usage.
RAZI:92:20/r9.anchor: يحيى بن وثاب : { إلا ابتغاء وجه ربه } بالرفع

TAB:92:20/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:20/r1.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:20/r1.claim: The giver spends neither to repay a human favor nor to receive human recompense, but gives in God's cause seeking his Lord's face; al-Ṭabarī says this reading is correct and supported by reports.
TAB:92:20/r1.anchor: كان بعض أهل العربية يوجه تأويل ذلك إلى :  وما لأحد من خلق الله عند هذا الذي يؤتى ماله في سبيل الله

TAB:92:20/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:20/r2.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:20/r2.claim: One Arabist takes illā here in the sense of “but.”
TAB:92:20/r2.anchor: قال :  وإلا في هذا الموضع بمعنى لكن وقال :  يجوز أن يكون الفعل

TAB:92:20/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:20/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:20/r3.claim: The Arabist allows the verb for repayment to be future, meaning the giver did not intend anyone's recompense for what he spent.
TAB:92:20/r3.anchor: وقال :  يجوز أن يكون الفعل في المكافأة مستقبلاً ،   فيكون معناه :  ولم يُرِد بما أنفق مكافأة من أحد

TAB:92:20/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:20/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB:92:20/r4.claim: The Arabist relates the lām in li-aḥadin to the pronoun in ʿindahu, construing the sense as no favor with anyone for which the giver seeks repayment.
TAB:92:20/r4.anchor: ويكون موقع اللام التي في أحد في الهاء التي خفضتها عنده ،   فكأنك قلت :  وما له عند أحد فيما أنفق

TAB:92:20/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:20/r5.speaker: author
TAB:92:20/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī endorses this Arabist construction; Arabs can place a particle away from its expected position when the intended relation is understood, as al-Nābigha's verse illustrates.
TAB:92:20/r5.anchor: وقد تضع العرب الحرف في غير موضعه إذا كان معروفا ،   واستشهدوا لذلك ببيت النابغة

TAB:92:20/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:20/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:92:20/r6.claim: Qatāda says the giving is for God rather than human reward; the verse concerns Abū Bakr, who freed six or seven people, including Bilāl and ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra, seeking neither repayment nor thanks.
TAB:92:20/r6.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  وَما لاِءَحَدٍ عِنْدَهُ مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ تُجْزَى قال :  نزلت في أبي بكر ،   أعتق ناسا لم يلتمس منهم جزاء ولا شكورا

TAB:92:20/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:20/r7.speaker: والد عامر بن عبد الله
TAB:92:20/r7.claim: The father of ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh reports that the verse was revealed about Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq.
TAB:92:20/r7.anchor: عن عامر بن عبد الله عن أبيه ،   قال :  نزلت هذه الآية في أبي بكر الصديق

BURHAN:v1p354/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p354/r2.speaker: بعض النحويين
BURHAN:v1p354/r2.claim: Some grammarians say a sentence's understood components allow stopping wherever one chooses, though the best pause is at the fullest meaning or a suitable estimate of it.
BURHAN:v1p354/r2.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين الجملة التأليفية إذا عرفت أجزاؤها وتكررت أركانها كان ما أدركه الحس فى حكم المذكور

BURHAN:v1p354/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p354/r3.speaker: الجمهور
BURHAN:v1p354/r3.claim: The majority classify Qur'anic pauses into complete, near-complete, deficient, good, near-good, bad, and near-bad, drawing on grammarians, readers, independent reasoning, and Prophetic practice such as stopping at verse endings.
BURHAN:v1p354/r3.anchor: وذهب الجمهور إلى أن الوقف فى التنزيل على ثمانية أضرب تام وشبيه به وناقص وحسن وشبيه به وقبيح وشبيه به

BURHAN:v1p354/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p354/r4.speaker: أبو يوسف القاضى
BURHAN:v1p354/r4.claim: Abū Yūsuf calls assigning Qur'anic pauses labels such as complete, deficient, good, or bad an innovation, since the entire Qur'an and each part are complete and good.
BURHAN:v1p354/r4.anchor: وذهب أبو يوسف القاضى صاحب أبى حنيفة إلى أن تقدير الموقوف عليه من القرآن التام والناقص والحسن والقبيح وتسميته بذلك بدعة

BURHAN:v1p354/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p354/r5.speaker: ابن الانبارى
BURHAN:v1p354/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī forbids pausing between syntactically dependent elements, including a genitive and its complement, a subject and predicate, a conjunction and its antecedent, or a relative pronoun and clause.
BURHAN:v1p354/r5.anchor: وقال ابن الانبارى لا يتم الوقف على المضاف دون المضاف إليه ولا على الرابع دون المرفوع ولا على المرفوع دون الرافع

BURHAN:v1p354/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p354/r6.speaker: أبو على
BURHAN:v1p354/r6.claim: Abū ʿAlī permits pausing before illā when it means 'but,' giving this verse's phrase as an example, along with other passages.
BURHAN:v1p354/r6.anchor: وجوز أبو على الوقف على ما قبل إلا إذا كانت بمعنى لكن

BURHAN:v4p235/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p235/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p235/r10.claim: ابتغاء وجه ربه is an exception because seeking the Lord's face is not of the same class as favors that are repaid.
BURHAN:v4p235/r10.anchor: فابتغاء وجه ربه ليس من جنس النعم التي تجزى

ITQAN:v3p16/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p16/r7.speaker: ابن اللبان
ITQAN:v3p16/r7.claim: Ibn al-Labbān interprets God's face in these expressions as sincerity of intention, including feeding for God's sake and seeking the Lord's face.
ITQAN:v3p16/r7.anchor: وقال ابن اللبان في قوله ﴿ يريدون وجهه ﴾ ﴿ إنما نطعمكم لوجه الله ﴾

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p271/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p271/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p271/r2.claim: In al-Aʿlā and al-Layl, al-aʿlā is not chosen in place of al-ʿulā merely to satisfy the verse ending.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p271/r2.anchor: ليست صيغة "الأعلى" معدولاً إليها فيهما عن العلىَّ لمجرد رعاية الفاصلة.
